subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Windshield Dangers
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Windshield Dangers.

hook.text: Early windshields were made of plain glass—the same kind used in house windows.

buildup.text: In a crash, the glass shattered into razor-sharp shards that sliced through passengers.

discovery.text: In 1903, a chemist dropped a flask coated in cellulose—it cracked but didn't shatter.

twist.text: This accident inspired laminated glass—two layers bonded with a plastic sheet between them.

climax.text: Ford adopted laminated windshields in 1927, and flying glass injuries dropped sharply.

punchline.text: A dropped flask saved millions of faces.

quiz.question: What inspired the invention of laminated windshield glass?
